html:
A large hydropower dam on the Blue Nile in western Ethiopia, close to the border with Sudan, built from 2011 to 2025. With 5.15 gigawatts of capacity it is the largest hydroelectric plant in Africa.

Prime Minister Meles Zenawi launched it in 2011. It was paid for mostly at home, through government bonds and contributions from Ethiopians, without big foreign loans. Meant to light a country where most people had no power, it became a symbol of national pride.

Downstream, Egypt depends on the Nile for nearly all its water, and the Blue Nile supplies most of the river's flow. Egypt feared that filling the reservoir fast would cut its share, and saw the dam as a threat to an order that colonial era treaties and its own Aswan High Dam had built in its favour. Sudan feared for its own dams. Years of talks brought no binding deal. Ethiopia filled the reservoir in five stages from 2020 to 2024, and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed formally opened the dam in 2025.
sum: A large hydropower dam on the Blue Nile in western Ethiopia, close to the border with Sudan, built from 2011 to 2025. With 5.15 gigawatts of capacity it is the largest hydroelectric plant in Africa.
